bio: Amitabh Bachchan, born on October 11, 1942 in Allahabad, India, is one of the most iconic and influential actors in Indian cinema. He made his film debut in 1969 with Saat Hindustani, but it was the film Zanjeer (1973) that established him as the 'Angry Young Man' of Bollywood. Over the decades, he has acted in more than 200 movies including blockbusters such as Sholay (1975), Deewar (1975), Amar Akbar Anthony (1977), Don (1978), Silsila (1981), Shahenshah (1988), Mohabbatein (2000), Black (2005), Paa (2009), and Pink (2016). His most popular and career-defining film is often considered to be Sholay (1975). Amitabh Bachchan is also a television personality and has been the host of 'Kaun Banega Crorepati' (the Indian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire) since 2000, which greatly revived his career. He has received numerous awards including the Padma Shri in 1984, Padma Bhushan in 2001, and Padma Vibhushan in 2015 from the Government of India. Internationally, he has been honored with the Knight of the Legion of Honour by France in 2007. Amitabh Bachchan married actress Jaya Bhaduri in 1973 and they have two children, Abhishek Bachchan and Shweta Bachchan. He currently resides in Mumbai, India at his famous bungalow 'Jalsa'. With a career spanning over five decades, Amitabh Bachchan is regarded as the Shahenshah of Bollywood and a living legend of Indian cinema.
